counterfactual_missing_items: Brain MRI and susceptibility-weighted imaging were unremarkable
fatigue test and a neostigmine test were both negative
Routine blood tests, coagulation studies, rheumatologic panels, thyroid function, tumor markers, liver and kidney function, and electrolytes were all normal
decisive_items: initial diagnosis was transient ischemic attack of the vertebrobasilar system
carotid MRA showed carotid arteriosclerosis with limited stenosis of the intracranial left vertebral artery;
response.rationale: R1 exactly matches the verbatim initial diagnosis and the episodic transient clinical picture. R2 substitutes 'insufficiency' for the explicitly stated TIA label, making it a less precise restatement. R4 and R7 are contradicted by unremarkable MRI/SWI and normal inflammatory workup; R5 describes underlying arteriosclerosis rather than the acute episodic diagnosis; C1 is a redundant episodic completion of R1.

rejected.why: Label 'Vertebrobasilar Insufficiency' is not verbatim; the raw support explicitly says transient ischemic attack, so this is a less precise restatement of R1.
Stroke is contradicted by unremarkable MRI/SWI and by fully resolving episodic symptoms without fixed deficit.
Cerebral vasculopathy/arteriosclerosis is an underlying vascular finding, not the acute episodic diagnosis.
Cerebral vasculitis is unsupported; MRI/SWI unremarkable and rheumatologic panels normal.
Append-only completion of R1; 'episodic' is already inherent in TIA and supported by the same span, so it adds no independent diagnostic information.
